findings.source_quote: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἔλθῃ, μενεῖς μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὧδε ἕως ἔρχεται.
findings.english_quote: If he does not come, you will stay here with us until he returns.
findings.issue: “Returns” introduces a previous presence at this location that this clause does not state. The selected Greek says “comes.” The source also explicitly uses a return verb for Hermas in paragraph 2, so translating this occurrence as “returns” obscures an observable distinction.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “If he does not come, you will stay here with us until he comes.”

findings.source_quote: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἔλθῃ, μενεῖς μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὧδε ἕως ἔρχεται.
findings.english_quote: If not, stay here with us until he returns.
findings.issue: Independently against the Greek, “returns” adds the implication that the shepherd has previously been at this location. The selected wording says “comes,” unlike the explicit return verb used for Hermas in paragraph 2. Simplification does not require adding that implication.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “If not, stay here with us until he comes.”

summary: Both editions cover all nine paragraphs and preserve the speakers, substantive negations, affectionate actions, brother/not-husband contrast, overnight prayer, time expression, and supper metaphor. Both need a small correction from “returns” to “comes” in paragraph 1. The notes distinguish reported editorial conjecture/restoration and the bracketed dance phrase rather than presenting everything as unqualified preserved manuscript text. This assessment concerns the supplied working Greek and attributed disclosures; it does not authenticate unseen editions or handwriting, independently verify the detailed apparatus attributions, or certify exhaustive collation. Proposed corrections remain subject to fresh review.
